definition: Two-model Bayesian optimization: Random Forest Regressor provides hypothetical predictions, Gaussian Process maximizes Expected Improvement acquisition function
assumptions: Adhesive strength is a smooth function of composition
Training data is representative of the accessible design space
invariants: Compositions must be non-negative and sum to unity
EI balances exploration (high uncertainty) and exploitation (high prediction)
Models are retrained with augmented data after each experimental round
non_negotiable_steps: Train surrogate model on experimental data
Generate candidate formulations satisfying compositional constraints
Compute Expected Improvement for all candidates
Select top candidates by EI and/or prediction for experimental validation
key_distinguishing_features: Hybrid RFR-GP approach: RFR for robust prediction, GP for uncertainty quantification
Protein-inspired monomer mapping: amino acid categories to synthetic monomers
deviations_from_original: Used 50,000 random Dirichlet candidates instead of exhaustive grid search
Added focused perturbations around top performers for better exploitation
Single SMBO run instead of 1000 repetitions for formula frequency analysis
